requirements.requirement: The 34-rune vocabulary is identified as governed owner-directed design rather than recovered source canon.
Source-specific spell, mana, resistance, counterspell, crafting, Overreach, Resonance, duration, range, damage, healing and XP fields remain owning-rule inputs.
PPIA-03, PPIA-08, PPIA-11, PPIA-12, F006/F007, F020 and F021 ownership boundaries remain explicit and nonabsorbed.
The final registry contains exactly 16 unique Operation Runes and 18 unique Essence Runes for 34 total core runes.
Operation Runes describe what magic does while Essence Runes fill typed payload/domain roles and are not standalone executable AST nodes.
No spell name automatically becomes a rune and the retained 385-spell catalog remains source content rather than being replaced by rune records.
THEN, WITH, WHEN and IF are the four explicit connection types and mixed connectors never receive implicit precedence.
Every valid visual graph round-trips to one canonical ordered linear serialization with equivalent AST meaning.
Invalid or ambiguous syntax fails before authoritative cost, effect or GM proposal creation and errors do not invent semantic outcomes.
Semantic evaluation classifies constructions as deterministic-supported, governed-adjudication-required, unresolved-owning-rule or invalid.
Valid open combinations may be GM-adjudicated without hallucinating missing damage, duration, template, destination, resistance or other authoritative game facts.
A valid Rune Construction never by itself guarantees affordability, success, target legality, lack of resistance or balance.
Rune Construction uses the 12 typed resource adapters and never introduces one universal cost equation.
Required unresolved adapters block or defer authoritative use according to owning rules rather than receiving guessed defaults.
Source-scoped resource values are preserved without automatic rune-wide repricing.
SCI remains a structural/cognitive complexity metric with simple, standard, advanced and expert bands and is not power.
CSL remains a structural stability-attention signal with baseline, watch, strained and high-attention bands and is not failure probability.
No automatic backlash, damage or failure table is inferred from SCI/CSL and final calibration remains with owning rules/PPIA-11.
Progressive disclosure teaches Operation Runes first, then Essence payload choices, then connectors and advanced architecture.
The four progression bands are guidance unless adopted by owning progression rules and do not silently create hard gameplay unlocks.
Conflicting Scripts & Macros progression values remain attributable rather than silently reconciled into universal Rune XP prices.
PPIA-07 owns rune-extension/validation semantics while PPIA-03 retains Item Definition and instance ownership.
Inscription compatibility, resources, SCI/CSL, predicted authorized effect, provenance and versions are inspectable before mutation.
Inscription/removal writes use expected-version and operation-ID recovery and cannot duplicate resource use or attached runes.
Rune resolution exposes recognize, resist, counter, sever-link, disable-trigger and dispel-or-remove hooks to owning rules.
UNMAKE, COMMAND, CALL, BANISH, SPACE and TIME do not bypass saves, resistance, source/destination validity or setting-local restrictions.
Blind mode may suppress counterplay evidence from the player but never removes it from authorized GM/authoritative resolution.
Standard-preview mode may show only permission-authorized semantic effect, costs, SCI/CSL, targets and rule references.
A standard preview is nonauthoritative and never commits an effect or consumes a resource by itself.
Whether standard play requires GM decision remains an owning Campaign/Action policy rather than a PPIA-07 shortcut.
In blind-gm-adjudicated mode the player can construct/serialize/validate/submit runes but cannot receive the interpreted or predicted magical effect before GM adjudication.
Blind-effect suppression is enforced through server-side role projection and cannot be bypassed by tooltips, counts, errors, history, export, diagnostics, notifications or player AI.
Post-resolution learning follows outcome-only, observed-details or full-after-resolution policy and successful use does not automatically reveal all rune mechanics.
An authorized GM receives a complete permission-safe effect card with decoded construction, interpreted result, targets, resources, SCI/CSL, counterplay, warnings, provenance and predicted mutations.
Blind final decisions are exactly approve, deny and modify-and-approve; silence or timeout is never approval.

Modify-and-approve preserves the immutable player expression and original resolved proposal plus exact diff/reasons; expression rewrites are explicit GM modifications and never attributed to the player.
Permission filtering precedes hidden runes, targets, anchors, channels, resources, semantic resolution, counts, queue entries, notifications, history, exports, diagnostics and AI context.
Unauthorized errors, counts, disabled states and timing-visible metadata cannot disclose protected rune/effect/target existence.
Blind-mode semantic suppression is an additional visibility boundary even when syntax and player-originated construction fields are visible.
Authoritative rune mutations, proposal submits, GM decisions and commits use stable operation identities and expected-version/current-version checks.
Ambiguous submit or decision responses query status with the original identity before retry and cannot duplicate proposals, effects, costs, inscriptions or notifications.
Stale actor, target, Session, resource, permission or rule state is revalidated and cannot silently become the accepted original proposal.
Every required visual graph, topology, shape, SCI/CSL view and GM effect card has an ordered semantic text/table equivalent usable by keyboard, touch and screen reader.
Blind gameplay never implies visual-only gameplay; accessibility output preserves permitted construction semantics without leaking suppressed interpreted effects.
Player-facing AI in blind mode may help syntax/accessibility but cannot decode hidden effects or predict GM approval; GM AI remains advisory and cannot decide or commit.
All original 20 grammar cases, 34 expanded-rune cases, 16 cost/stability benchmarks, 16 workflows, 18 actions, 10 handoffs and 16 blind-play cases remain represented in the completion contract.
The 385-spell source audit retains 10 schools, 7 roles, 14 effect families, 22 subtype families and zero vocabulary-level unroutable spell IDs.
Completion does not activate application runtime, STAGE-A-A2, release, deployment, tester access, paid services, production credentials or unsupported canonical promotion.
